title: Efficient Caching with A Tag-enhanced DRAM
problem: DRAM-based caches (e.g., HBM3-as-cache) suffer from high miss penalties due to two-step tag-then-data access, wasted data movement on cache misses where data is fetched then discarded, and interference between demand requests and miss-fetched data on the data bus. Existing DRAM cache designs cannot perform in-DRAM tag comparison or conditional data response, so they always transfer data regardless of hit/miss status.
motivation: SRAM caches are hitting a density scaling wall, driving adoption of DRAM-based caches (HBM, LPDDR) for large-footprint workloads, but DRAM cache performance is limited by the fundamental mismatch between DRAM's architecture and cache semantics (tag checks, conditional data return, dirty data management).
method: TDRAM embeds small, fast lookup tables (called tag mats) directly on the HBM3 memory chip, enabling it to check whether requested data is cached internally and send data only on hits—eliminating wasted transfers on misses. Early tag probing begins lookups before the full memory row is ready, reducing latency on both hits and misses. A flush buffer (temporary storage in the DRAM) holds dirty data (modified but not yet saved), avoiding delays from writing old data back before fetching new data.
key_novelty: Adding low-latency tag lookup tables (tag mats) directly to the HBM3 DRAM die enables in-DRAM tag comparison and conditional data response—data transfers to the CPU only on cache hits—matching SRAM cache behavior by eliminating wasted bandwidth on misses.
contributions: TDRAM microarchitecture adding on-die tag mats to HBM3 for in-DRAM tag comparison and conditional data response
Opportunistic early tag probing reducing latency for both hit and miss paths
In-DRAM flush buffer eliminating data bus turnaround delays on write misses
2.65x faster tag checks, 1.23x speedup, and 21% less energy vs state-of-the-art DRAM cache designs across HPC workloads

metrics.speedup: 1.23x speedup vs state-of-the-art commercial and research DRAM caches

limitations: Not discussed; adding tag mats to HBM3 increases die area and manufacturing complexity, and potential impact on HBM3 density/cost is not quantified.
primary_theme: in-DRAM tag comparison for efficient DRAM-based cache with conditional data response
